title: dispatch
description: Input schema for the litany built-in `dispatch` tool (ARCH §2.5, §3.3, §3.4 — v0.4 Phase 2). The harness sends this verbatim as the `input_schema` field of the tool's entry in the model call's `tools: [...]` array.

role.description: Subagent role to dispatch. The role set is open (ARCH §4.3): a role is dispatchable iff the governing config commit lists it under the `roles:` block of `providers.yaml` and carries its `souls/<role>.md`, and the harness enumerates no role names. A role failing either check is refused before the child's branch exists, naming the pool that is defined.

goal.description: Per-dispatch goal text. Written verbatim to the subagent's goal.md on its dispatch commit (ARCH §2.3 step 2 / §2.8). The subagent reads its goal there; the dispatching agent does not see the subagent's intermediate work — only its terminal response, which returns later as a message deposited into the parent's inbox alongside the epitaph naming how the agent ended (ARCH §2.6, §2.11). A subagent is an ordinary agent and the dispatch is not one-shot: `message` reaches it at any step boundary while it runs, and it may dispatch subagents of its own up to the tree's `max_depth` (ARCH §6).

name.description: Display name for the child (ARCH §2.3): one unbroken word, unique among the workspace's living agents, set here and never rewritten. A name is the child's identity in every surface — it is stored under the child, told to the child itself, and is what `message` accepts in place of the child's agent id — so supplying one keeps the identities and tasks in a subagent tree clear; pick a name that says what the child is for. If you omit it, a valid two-word PascalCase name is minted automatically (`PeachHollow`), so an unnamed dispatch is never an error — but a name you supply that is malformed, begins like an agent id, or is already worn by a living agent is refused and no child is created.
